description.value: The study examined how motivational dispositions measured by BIS/BAS scales modulate neural responses during cognitive reappraisal in currently drug-free patients with major depressive disorder compared with healthy controls.

spans.text: Second, to test the hypothesis that motivation dispositions differentially modulated reappraisal-related brain responses in two groups, we conducted a voxel-wise analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) with group, emotion and ER as between-subject factors and BIS/BAS subscale scores as covariates.

design.value: A block-design fMRI study compared depressed patients and healthy controls during attend, detach, and immerse emotion-regulation conditions, with BIS/BAS motivation scores entered as covariates and predictors of neural responses.

spans.text: The task was performed in three consecutive blocks (“ATTEND,” “DETACH,” and “IMMERSE”).
Block design was utilized to avoid potential task-switching effects that might obscure differences between regulation and passive viewing conditions (Moser et al., 2010 ).
Pictures of stimuli were selected from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS) (Lang et al., 2008 ) based on normative ratings and were matched for content of scenes and people (Table S1 ).

task_description.value: Participants viewed positive, negative, and neutral emotional pictures while attending naturally, detaching from the depicted situation, or immersing themselves in it, and rated emotional intensity.

spans.text: During the ATTEND block (as baseline condition), the subjects responded naturally without trying to change the emotional state elicited by the stimuli.
During the DETACH block (avoidance-oriented reappraisal), participants were asked to interpret the situation depicted as fake or unreal
During the IMMERSE block (approach-oriented reappraisal), subjects were asked to perceive each picture as real by imagining themselves or a loved one in the scene.
Block design was utilized to avoid potential task-switching effects
The protocol for the paradigm was administered using the commercial software package E-Prime 2.0 (standard version).

instructions.value: Attend naturally; detach by interpreting the situation as fake or unreal; immerse by perceiving each picture as real and imagining oneself or a loved one in the scene.

spans.text: During the DETACH block (avoidance-oriented reappraisal), participants were asked to interpret the situation depicted as fake or unreal, as would someone with no personal attachment to the events.
During the IMMERSE block (approach-oriented reappraisal), subjects were asked to perceive each picture as real by imagining themselves or a loved one in the scene.

description.value: The first trial of each block was discarded; volumes underwent slice-timing correction, realignment, normalization to standard MNI space, and 8-mm FWHM spatial smoothing.

spans.text: The first trial of each block (attend/detach/immerse condition) was discarded to reach the magnetization equilibrium. The remaining volumes were corrected for slice timing, and then realigned to the mean volume to correct for head motion. Images were spatially normalized to the standard MNI space using a 12-parameter affine transformation, and smoothed by convolution with a standard 8-mm full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) isotropic Gaussian kernel.
All functional and structural image processing and statistical analyses were conducted with SPM8
